findings.title: Heap buffer overflow in argon2i_32 from unvalidated nb_blocks
findings.evidence: argon2i_32 (c_monocypher.pyx:322) takes caller-supplied nb_blocks and assigns it straight into config.nb_blocks at line 328 with no range check, while the password/salt/key/ad lengths are validated by _validate_u32. Line 345 then allocates work_area = malloc(nb_blocks * 1024) and line 347 hands that buffer to crypto_argon2. Monocypher's own contract (monocypher.h:160) requires nb_blocks >= 8 * nb_lanes, and nb_lanes is hard-coded to 1 at line 330, so any nb_blocks < 8 is invalid; the C implementation nevertheless starts by unconditionally writing two 1024-byte blocks per lane (monocypher.c:776-783, blocks[l*lane_size + i] for i in {0,1}) before any count-dependent loop. For nb_blocks=1 only 1024 bytes are allocated but blocks[1] is written at offset 1024-2047 -> 1024-byte heap overflow; for nb_blocks=0 malloc(0) is used and blocks[0]/blocks[1] are still written. For nb_blocks=2 or 3 segment_size/lane_size round down to 0, so monocypher.c:902 computes last_block = blocks - 1 and reads/writes before the allocation (monocypher.c:902-915). An attacker controlling the work factor (e.g. a remotely supplied KDF parameter) reaches heap corruption/DoS; fixed upstream in 4.0.2.8 by adding this very check after config.nb_lanes = 1.
